Science.title: Lumina simulation brings the early universe to life on a record-breaking scale
Science.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Nancy Roman Space Telescope are revealing the universe's earliest chapters in detail. To help astronomers understand what they are seeing, researchers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian have developed "Lumina," one of the largest and most detailed simulations ever created of the early universe.

Science.title: Scientists discover how pancreatic cancer rewrites its DNA to escape treatment
Science.summary: Scientists have discovered how pancreatic cancer cells continually reshape their genetic makeup to become more aggressive, spread, and evade treatment. In laboratory experiments, blocking a key gene reversed some of these dangerous changes, revealing a potential new way to fight the deadly disease.

Science.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
Science.summary: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.

Science.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
Science.summary: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.

Science.title: Protecting children from harm isn't enough—welfare systems must support healing through quality mental health care
Science.summary: In Quebec and across Canada, people working in child welfare do remarkable work to protect children and youth from maltreatment and to support families facing complex challenges.

Science.title: Patterns of polar vortices discovered in lead-free superlattices on silicon
Science.summary: A team at HZB has, for the first time, reported polar vortices in (BaTiO₃/SrTiO₃)₁₀ superlattices on silicon. These results expand the range of materials and substrates on which polar topological textures can occur and open up new options for incorporating complex ferroelectric states into silicon-based technologies.

Science.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
Science.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect. The discovery suggests that genetics could help explain why some people benefit while others do not.

Science.title: Scientists discover a hidden flaw that challenges 40 years of superconductor science
Science.summary: A superconducting material studied for 40 years has turned out to be far more complex than scientists believed. Advanced 3D imaging revealed a hidden patchwork of crystal structures, with unusually wide boundaries that may weaken superconductivity. The discovery challenges decades of scientific assumptions and could explain why some superconductors outperform others.

Science.title: Who should have a say in which species are saved? The California condor offers lessons for a global biodiversity treaty
Science.summary: In 1987, biologists captured the last free-flying condor to transfer it to captivity, and the largest flying North American bird species was officially declared extinct in the wild. Today, after decades of coordinated efforts and millions of dollars spent on captive breeding and reintroduction efforts, more than 300 condors have been restored to their natural environment.

Science.title: Milky Way's disk grew 'upside down,' with younger stars forming in ever-thinner layers
Science.summary: The Milky Way is home to hundreds of billions of stars arranged in a glorious spiral pattern. But beyond the obvious spiral, our galaxy has other physical characteristics. It's divided into a galactic bulge, a galactic disk and a galactic halo.

Science.title: Crows make decisions twice as fast as humans and monkeys
Science.summary: University of Tübingen researchers have shown that crows, when confronted with a visual choice, make a decision twice as fast as humans and monkeys. In the experiment, two carrion crows took just 235 milliseconds on average to identify the direction in which a dot pattern was moving and to indicate their choice—while maintaining a high degree of accuracy.

Science.title: ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11328-3 ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2

Science.title: How purported tales of consuming vampire blood and organs spread in the 18th century
Science.summary: In this excerpt from "Killing the Dead," author John Blair looks at how the printed press ramped up tales of vampirism, leading to stories of people eating a supposed vampire's organs and drinking their blood in a bid to avoid the same fate.

Science.title: This mysterious mushroom makes people see hundreds of tiny humans
Science.summary: For nearly a century, people in distant parts of the world have reported a bizarre experience after eating certain wild mushrooms: seeing dozens or even hundreds of tiny, colorful humans moving through the real world. Now, scientists have identified a mushroom species, Lanmaoa asiatica, responsible for these extraordinary hallucinations in China and the Philippines.

Science.title: Supercurrent enables the reading of quantum information without destroying it
Science.summary: One of the fundamental challenges of quantum computing is obtaining information from a quantum bit, or qubit. Unlike a conventional bit, which can be read repeatedly without altering its content, direct measurement of a quantum system typically causes the state to collapse before it can be determined. In other words, reading the information modifies it.

Science.title: Sea cucumber–inspired gel could help heal damaged tissue in humans
Science.summary: Inspired by the ability of sea cucumbers to change the stiffness of their bodies, University of Waterloo researchers have developed a gel that could one day help repair damaged tendons and other soft tissues without leaving permanent material behind.

Science.title: Bell pepper colors reveal differences in sweetness, nutrients and ripeness
Science.summary: Raw, grilled, roasted, stuffed—there are many ways to enjoy bell peppers, also called capsicums, sweet peppers or paprika. Bell peppers originated in Central and South America and belong to the nightshade family along with tomatoes and eggplants.

Science.title: Tests reveal why titanium additions do not fully prevent pitting corrosion in stainless steel
Science.summary: Stainless steel is widely used for its corrosion resistance, but it is not invincible. In environments containing chloride ions, such as seawater, pitting corrosion can occur. These pits often start at tiny particles called inclusions embedded in the steel.

Science.title: Cosmic 'seagull' locks eyes with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in long-awaited test image
Science.summary: Stare into the transfixing eye of the "Seagull Nebula" in this newly-released test image from the visionary Vera C. Rubin Observatory.

Science.title: A few seconds of loading time can push online learners off track
Science.summary: An online lesson takes an extra second to load. The wait may seem trivial, but in a study examining large learning platforms, these brief pauses were linked to unfinished assignments, lower scores and less time spent on the site.

Science.title: Scientists Trapped an Antimatter Particle for Months to Study Its Secrets
Science.summary: These elusive and reactive particles have been challenging to hold on to and even more challenging to study, but a new method paves the way for tests on the differences between matter and antimatter.

Science.title: What happened when humans encountered Gigantopithecus?
Science.summary: Gigantopithecus was the largest primate that ever lived. What would have happened when human ancestors encountered it?

Science.title: Monarchs report their locations via… cellphone?
Science.summary: Who knew a monarch butterfly could borrow a cellphone to check in with friendly people he met on his journey? That is essentially what happens now that new technology has reduced the weight of a radio-pulse tag to less than half a gram (0.02 ounces).
